title: Checkpoint Loading Errors (missing_keys, unexpected_keys, size mismatch)
description: Troubleshooting and resolving state dict loading errors in deep learning frameworks, including missing keys, unexpected keys, and size mismatches.
name: Checkpoint Loading Errors (missing_keys, unexpected_keys, size mismatch)

quick_identification.description: Checkpoint is missing parameters present in the model.
Checkpoint contains parameters not present in the model.

quick_identification.check: load_state_dict() raises RuntimeError with size mismatch
quick_identification.description: Checkpoint tensor shape differs from the model parameter shape.

quick_identification.check: Model loads with strict=False but outputs are wrong
quick_identification.description: Silent partial load leaves some layers at initialization.

symptoms.description: RuntimeError lists keys present in the model but absent from the checkpoint state dict.
symptoms.error_message: RuntimeError: Error(s) in loading state_dict: Missing key(s) in state_dict: "layer.weight", "layer.bias".

symptoms.description: RuntimeError lists keys present in the checkpoint but absent from the model.
symptoms.error_message: RuntimeError: Error(s) in loading state_dict: Unexpected key(s) in state_dict: "module.layer.weight".

symptoms.description: Tensor shape in the checkpoint does not match the model parameter shape.
symptoms.error_message: RuntimeError: Error(s) in loading state_dict: size mismatch for layer.weight: copying a param with shape torch.Size([768, 512]) from checkpoint, the shape in current model is torch.Size([1024, 512]).

symptoms.description: Checkpoint loads with strict=False, but some layers retain random initialization.
symptoms.error_message: No explicit error; model outputs are degraded or random.

root_causes.explanation: DistributedDataParallel wraps the model in a module. namespace; a checkpoint saved from DDP includes that prefix, and loading into a non-DDP model produces key mismatches.
recognition_clues: Unexpected keys all start with module..
Checkpoint was saved from DDP training and loaded for single-GPU inference.
missing_keys and unexpected_keys are symmetric with and without module..
root_causes.typical_environment: Distributed training checkpoints loaded for single-GPU inference, DDP to non-DDP transitions.

root_causes.explanation: The model structure changed after the checkpoint was saved, so the state dict no longer matches the parameter graph.
recognition_clues: size mismatch on specific modified layers.
Missing keys for newly added layers.
Model config differs from checkpoint config, such as hidden_size changes.
root_causes.typical_environment: Fine-tuning with custom heads, pruning, distillation, progressive resizing.

root_causes.cause: Sharded vs. Full State Dict Mismatch
root_causes.explanation: FSDP or DeepSpeed may save sharded checkpoints per rank, but the loader expects a full state dict, or the reverse.
recognition_clues: Checkpoint directory contains multiple rank-suffixed .pt files.
load_state_dict() fails with file-not-found or partial key errors.
World size differs between save and load.
root_causes.typical_environment: FSDP with sharded state dicts, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, multi-node training resume.

root_causes.explanation: Model weights load successfully, but optimizer state dict keys or parameter groups no longer match the current training setup.
recognition_clues: optimizer.load_state_dict() fails after the model loads.
Errors mention param_groups or state.
Scheduler state no longer matches the current step count.
root_causes.typical_environment: Resume after hyperparameter changes, optimizer swaps, warm restarts.

root_causes.explanation: Framework upgrades can change state dict conventions, hook behavior, or serialization expectations across versions.
recognition_clues: Missing keys follow a systematic naming pattern.
Checkpoint was saved with an older framework version.
Release notes or migration guidance mention state dict behavior changes.
root_causes.typical_environment: PyTorch 1.x to 2.x migrations, Transformers 3.x to 4.x upgrades, model hub downloads with outdated format.

root_causes.cause: Adapter or LoRA Checkpoint with Wrong Base Model
root_causes.explanation: A PEFT adapter checkpoint is paired with a different base model architecture, so adapter and base keys do not align.
recognition_clues: load_adapter() fails with missing keys.
base_model_name_or_path differs from the loaded base.
LoRA ranks or target modules do not match.
root_causes.typical_environment: Multi-adapter serving, adapter merging, cross-model adapter transfer.

root_causes.explanation: The checkpoint write was interrupted, producing a truncated or corrupted file that cannot be read correctly.
recognition_clues: File size is unexpectedly small.
torch.load() raises pickle.UnpicklingError or EOFError.
The checkpoint was written before a crash or preemption.
root_causes.typical_environment: Spot instances, preemptible VMs, checkpointing under memory pressure.

investigation_checklist.check: Check checkpoint key names vs. model keys

investigation_checklist.description: Verify whether the checkpoint has a module. wrapper and the target model does not, or vice versa.

investigation_checklist.check: Check model config against checkpoint config
investigation_checklist.description: Compare model.config with the saved config for architecture divergence.
Determine whether the checkpoint is sharded via FSDP or DeepSpeed, or stored as a full state dict.

investigation_checklist.check: Check framework versions at save vs. load
investigation_checklist.description: Compare PyTorch and Transformers versions across save and load events.
If resuming training, verify the optimizer state matches the model parameter graph.
Verify file size and attempt torch.load() before attaching it to a model.

diagnostic_commands.command: python -c "ckpt = torch.load('checkpoint.pt'); model_keys = set(model.state_dict().keys()); ckpt_keys = set(ckpt.keys()); print(f'Missing: {model_keys - ckpt_keys}'); print(f'Unexpected: {ckpt_keys - model_keys}')"
diagnostic_commands.expected_output: Empty sets for an exact match.
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: Non-empty sets indicate key naming or architecture mismatch.

diagnostic_commands.command: python -c "ckpt = torch.load('checkpoint.pt', map_location='cpu'); print(ckpt.keys() if isinstance(ckpt, dict) else type(ckpt)); print(f'Model keys: {len(ckpt.get(\"model\", ckpt))}')"
diagnostic_commands.expected_output: A dictionary with model, optimizer, and scheduler keys for training checkpoints.
diagnostic_commands.interpretation: Unexpected structure indicates a custom checkpoint format or corruption.

diagnostic_commands.command: python -c "for k in ckpt: if k in model.state_dict(): print(f'{k}: ckpt={ckpt[k].shape}, model={model.state_dict()[k].shape}')"
diagnostic_commands.expected_output: Matching shapes for all shared keys.

diagnostic_commands.command: python -c "import os; size = os.path.getsize('checkpoint.pt'); print(f'Size: {size} bytes'); ckpt = torch.load('checkpoint.pt', map_location='cpu'); print('Load OK')"
diagnostic_commands.expected_output: A reasonable file size and no exceptions.

diagnostic_tests.test: Strip module. from checkpoint keys and attempt reload.
diagnostic_tests.command: python -c "ckpt = torch.load('checkpoint.pt'); stripped = {k.replace('module.', ''): v for k, v in ckpt.items()}; model.load_state_dict(stripped, strict=False)"
diagnostic_tests.expected_result: Load succeeds with no missing or unexpected keys.
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: If load succeeds, DDP prefixing was the issue.

diagnostic_tests.test: Compare saved config with current model config.
diagnostic_tests.command: python -c "import json; saved_cfg = json.load(open('config.json')); curr_cfg = model.config.to_dict(); diff = {k: (saved_cfg.get(k), curr_cfg.get(k)) for k in set(saved_cfg) | set(curr_cfg) if saved_cfg.get(k) != curr_cfg.get(k)}; print(diff)"
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: Non-empty diff shows architecture divergence causing size mismatch.
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Revert config changes or implement selective weight loading.

diagnostic_tests.test: Check whether silent partial load is occurring with strict=False.
diagnostic_tests.command: python -c "missing, unexpected = model.load_state_dict(ckpt, strict=False); print(f'Missing: {len(missing)}, Unexpected: {len(unexpected)}'); print(f'Missing layers: {missing}')"
diagnostic_tests.interpretation: Non-empty lists indicate layers using random initialization.
diagnostic_tests.next_action: Fix key mapping or explicitly initialize missing layers.

decision_tree.question: Does the error mention Missing key(s) in state_dict?

yes.question: Do missing keys follow the pattern module.X while the model has X?

yes.result: DDP module. prefix mismatch — strip the prefix or load into the DDP wrapper.

no.question: Are missing keys newly added layers that are not in the checkpoint?

yes.result: Architecture modification — initialize missing layers manually or use strict=False with explicit init.

no.question: Did the framework version change between save and load?

yes.result: Version migration naming change — implement key remapping.

no.result: Corrupted or wrong checkpoint — verify the checkpoint source.

no.question: Does the error mention Unexpected key(s) in state_dict?

yes.question: Do unexpected keys follow the pattern module.X?

yes.result: Loading a DDP checkpoint into a non-DDP model — strip module. prefix.

no.result: Checkpoint has extra parameters such as optimizer state or EMA — filter keys or load with strict=False.

no.question: Does the error mention size mismatch?

yes.question: Is the mismatch in the embedding layer?

yes.result: Vocabulary size change — resize embeddings or remap token IDs.

no.result: Architecture dimension change such as hidden_size or num_heads — load compatible layers only and reinitialize changed layers.

yes.result: Checkpoint corruption — restore from backup or retrain.

no.result: Unknown issue — inspect checkpoint structure manually.

solutions.quick_fix: Remove the module. prefix from checkpoint keys before loading.
solutions.permanent_fix: Save checkpoints from model.module.state_dict() when using DDP.
steps: Identify the prefix: all(k.startswith('module.') for k in checkpoint.keys()).
Strip the prefix: checkpoint = {k.replace('module.', ''): v for k, v in checkpoint.items()}.
Load the stripped checkpoint: model.load_state_dict(checkpoint).
For future runs, modify the save hook to unwrap DDP before state dict extraction.
tradeoffs: Forgetting to strip causes repeated failures.
works_for: Single-GPU inference from distributed training checkpoints.

solutions.solution: Load with strict=False and Initialize Missing Layers
solutions.quick_fix: Use strict=False and manually initialize layers not present in the checkpoint.
solutions.permanent_fix: Implement selective loading with explicit initialization logic.
steps: Load with permissive mode: missing, unexpected = model.load_state_dict(ckpt, strict=False).
Identify missing layers: print(missing).
Initialize missing layers with the model’s default init or module-specific init.
For changed dimensions, load compatible sub-tensors via slicing or interpolation.
Log loaded versus initialized parameters for audit.
tradeoffs: Silent failures if unexpected keys are actually important.
New layers start from scratch and may need more training.
solutions.performance_impact: None for loading; may need longer fine-tuning.
works_for: Transfer learning with custom top layers.
solutions.verification: All model parameters have non-zero gradients after the first backward pass.

solutions.solution: Remap Keys for Framework Version Migration
solutions.quick_fix: Create a key mapping dictionary and transform the checkpoint.
solutions.permanent_fix: Use built-in migration utilities or conversion scripts where provided.
steps: Identify naming changes from release notes.
Build a mapping dictionary such as key_map = {'old_name': 'new_name', ...}.
Transform the checkpoint using that mapping.
Handle split or merged parameters such as combined QKV.
Validate shapes after remapping.
tradeoffs: Requires understanding of framework-internal naming conventions.
May not cover all edge cases in custom architectures.
solutions.verification: All keys load without missing or unexpected entries after remapping.

solutions.solution: Convert Sharded to Full State Dict
solutions.quick_fix: Use FSDP full-state-dict settings before loading.
solutions.permanent_fix: Standardize on full state dicts for checkpoints that must move across environments.
steps: For FSDP, configure full-state-dict behavior before saving or loading.
Save the resulting full state dict.
Load it with standard model.load_state_dict().
For DeepSpeed, use the provided conversion script to obtain a consolidated model checkpoint.
tradeoffs: Full state dict requires enough CPU RAM to hold the entire model.
Sharded checkpoints are faster to save and load in distributed settings.
solutions.performance_impact: Higher memory usage during save and load; no training impact.
works_for: FSDP or DeepSpeed checkpoints loaded on a single GPU.
solutions.verification: A single checkpoint loads successfully on a non-distributed setup.

solutions.solution: Load Compatible Layers Only with Slicing
solutions.quick_fix: Load matching shapes and slice or interpolate mismatched tensors.
solutions.permanent_fix: Implement custom loading logic for known architecture variants.
steps: Iterate over checkpoint keys.
If a shape matches, copy it directly.
If a shape differs, slice the overlapping dimensions or interpolate where appropriate.
For attention heads, reshape and load compatible subsets.
Log which layers were sliced versus fully loaded.
tradeoffs: Sliced layers may not preserve full representational capacity.
solutions.performance_impact: None for loading; may affect model capacity.
solutions.verification: Loaded layers have expected values and newly sized dimensions are properly initialized.

Model produces the same output as before save
verification_checklist.description: Forward pass on a fixed input matches pre-save output.

verification_checklist.check: Optimizer state loads correctly if resuming training
verification_checklist.description: optimizer.load_state_dict() succeeds and step count is preserved.

verification_checklist.check: Training loss matches the pre-checkpoint trajectory
verification_checklist.description: Loss curve is continuous across the checkpoint boundary.

practices: Always save checkpoints from unwrapped models, such as model.module.state_dict() in DDP.
Include model config alongside the checkpoint for architecture verification.
Version-pin PyTorch and Transformers in training environments.
Use safetensors when corruption resistance is important.
Save both full and sharded checkpoints if cross-environment loading is expected.
Validate checkpoint integrity immediately after save by attempting a reload in the same job.
Store checkpoint metadata such as framework versions, git commit, and config hash.
Use torch.save() with robust serialization settings appropriate to your PyTorch version.
Alert when checkpoint load fails in the inference pipeline.
Track checkpoint save success and failure rates.
Monitor checkpoint file sizes for anomalies such as unexpected shrinkage.
Log key counts and parameter counts at save and load time.
Never use strict=False without explicitly inspecting missing and unexpected keys.
Implement checkpoint loading wrappers that validate config compatibility.
Add try/except around load_state_dict() with informative error messages.
Use model.save_pretrained() and from_pretrained() for Hugging Face models instead of manual state dict management when applicable.

common_misconceptions.misconception: strict=False is a safe way to load any checkpoint
common_misconceptions.reality: It silently skips mismatches, so layers may remain randomly initialized without warning.

common_misconceptions.misconception: DDP checkpoints are incompatible with single-GPU inference
common_misconceptions.reality: Only the module. prefix differs, and it can be stripped or avoided by saving the unwrapped model.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Checkpoint corruption always causes immediate load failure
common_misconceptions.reality: Partial corruption may load but still produce wrong outputs, so outputs should be validated after load.

false_positive_cases.case: Intentional partial load for layer freezing
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Code explicitly filters keys for frozen layers and sets requires_grad=False.

false_positive_cases.case: EMA weights in the checkpoint are not needed for inference
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: EMA keys are expected and can be filtered out or used for inference.

false_positive_cases.case: Quantized model loading into a non-quantized architecture
false_positive_cases.how_to_distinguish: Keys have quantization-specific suffixes and require a matching quantization config.

escalation_paths.when_to_use: The checkpoint is corrupted but raw parameter files still exist.
tradeoffs: May lose optimizer state and training metadata.

escalation_paths.when_to_use: No recoverable state exists and corruption is severe.
A bug is suspected in load_state_dict() or from_pretrained().
tradeoffs: Fix may not be available until a later release.
